text:
marco: quick RFC follow-up: we need a decision on what the SDK should do when a tenant is resident-only and the primary region is down. retry? surface error? offer escrow flow via SDK?
ellis: tl;dr: SDK should be conservative by default (surface an error), and offer opt-in helpers for enterprise customers.

shreya: concern: many customers call the SDK from client apps and will expect transparent failover. we must avoid making SDKs silently violate residency.

legal-bot: policy: do not allow automatic cross-region processing for resident data without a consent token. Any SDK convenience must require the explicit consent token and record where it came from.

ops: operational ask: if SDKs expose an "auto-escrow" helper we need observability hooks (eg telemetry event :residency:escrow_attempt) so we can detect mass forwardings during a region outage.

sdk-team: proposal for SDK behavior (default + opt-ins):
1) default: raise ResidencyError with code RESIDENCY_BLOCKED. Include server-suggested remediation (set header or contact support).
2) opt-in: provide method allow_residency_fallback(consent_token, mode) where mode in {proxy_sync, execute_escrow, proxy_defer}.
3) when allow_residency_fallback used, SDK logs a structured telemetry event with consent_id, tenant_id (if present), mode, and request_id.

marco: sample JS usage idea:
```
const client = new Redwood({apiKey});
client.setResidenceFallback({mode: 'execute_escrow', consentToken: 'CONSENT::t-123::c-456::168...'});
await client.generate({tenantId: 't-123', prompt});
```

ellis: runtime notes: execute_escrow returns 202 with escrow_token and X-Redwood-Finality: pending. SDK should surface this as a PendingResult object and provide .waitForFinality(escrow_token) helper that polls reconciliation status.

shreya: UX: warn integrators that using fallback may surface non-final responses to end-users. recommend a two-tier UX: show a preview with pending badge, final result replaces preview when reconciled.

legal-bot: consent token schema reminder: CONSENT::{tenant}::{consent_id}::{ts}::{scopes}. SDK must only accept tokens issued by our consent-service (validate via introspect endpoint). SDK introspect call must be rate-limited.

ops: metrics we need from SDKs and runtime: residency_sdk_fallback_attempts, residency_sdk_fallback_success, residency_pending_count, residency_replay_failures. Tag by region and tenant-tier.

sdk-team: about idempotency: SDKs should set idempotency_key by default (uuid v4) on all mutating requests. This protects against double-apply during reconciliation. We'll add helper middleware.

marco: question: billing and visibility: if SDK triggers standby execution, do we surface billing event immediately? customers asked to see a clear line item.

ellis: yes, runtime bills at execution time. SDK can fetch a billing-preview endpoint with the estimated token cost when fallback is about to be used; include it in the PendingResult so UIs can show "this may cost X and be non-final".

shreya: caution: embeddings and vector stores for resident tenants must not replicate until final. SDK should surface a flag in the embedding API response header X-Redwood-Finality: pending|final and block automatic upstream replication helpers.

legal-bot: also require consent audit binding: SDK must store (locally) the consent_id and the consent timestamp for 30 days to help customers during audits. But company retention is 7 years on server side.

ops: runbook snippet for large outages: if residency_pending_count > 100k and avg_replay_age > 10m then we should flip global feature-flag to disallow execute_escrow (admin-kill) and notify account teams. SDK telemetry helps trigger this.

marco: decision summary (quick): default SDK: fail-fast with clear ResidencyError. SDK helpers: opt-in allow_residency_fallback(consent_token, mode) + idempotency_key + waitForFinality. Obs + billing preview required. Owners?

sdk-team: we'll own SDK changes + telemetry + docs.

ellis: runtime will own billing preview + finality endpoints + escrow state.

ops: runbook + alarms = ops.

legal-bot: consent service + audit retention = legal.

sam.k: timeline: SDK patch + docs in 2 weeks, runtime preview endpoint spike next week. Can everyone ack?

sdk-team: ack.

ellis: ack.

shreya: ack, will update product notes.

marco: thanks all. closing when SDK PR lands.
